messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failure relates to the handling of array classes in ClassUtils methods like getShortClassName and getPackageName. From the current bug report, it is clear that getShortClassName adds an unwanted semicolon at the end for array types. 

Inspecting the snippet for getShortClassName(Object, String), we see it delegates to getShortClassName(Class<?>), which calls getShortClassName(String) by passing the class name.

The key logic is in getShortClassName(String), where array encoding is mentioned in comments but there is no implemented code to actually strip or handle array type encoding such as brackets or semicolons introduced by the Java class name of arrays (e.g., [Ljava.lang.String;). The method simply finds the last '.' and returns the substring after it, replacing '$' with '.'. This will cause array class names, which have differing formats, to be malformed or include extra characters.

Similarly, getPackageName(Class<?>) delegates to getPackageName(String), which also has comments about stripping array encoding but does not implement any stripping logic; it just returns the substring before the last '.' without accounting for array notations.

For example, the class name for String[] is "[Ljava.lang.String;", and the methods do not clean this up before extracting short class name or package, leading to the semicolon seen in the bug report.

Therefore, the root cause is the lack of proper handling and normalization of array class names (encoding) in the getShortClassName(String) and getPackageName(String) methods. This results in wrong outputs when those methods are called with arrays.

Recent reports do not appear related since they concern other utility issues, so this diagnosis mainly relies on the current report and the examined code snippets.

Next, we can recommend fixes to these methods to parse and remove array encoding characters before extracting the short name or package name.

Classes and methods relevant for fixing:
- ClassUtils.getShortClassName(String)
- ClassUtils.getPackageName(String)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
